answer: FRED could not be reached (every call returned Access Denied), so this is from memory, not from FRED: the effective federal funds rate averaged about 19.04% in July 1981. Source would be the Federal Reserve Board (H.15), FRED series FEDFUNDS.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED: the median sales price of houses sold in the U.S. in Q4 2022 is about $442,600 in the revised data as I recall it; it was first published as $479,500. I could not confirm which figure FRED shows today. Source would be the Census Bureau and HUD, FRED series MSPUS.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED: the U.S. unemployment rate averaged about 3.7% over the 12 months of 2019 (seasonally adjusted monthly rates ranged from about 3.5% to 4.0%). Source would be the Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series UNRATE.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED: year-over-year headline CPI inflation was above 4% in 5 months of 2023, January through May (roughly 6.4%, 6.0%, 5.0%, 4.9% and 4.1%). May is a borderline case at about 4.05-4.1%, so I could not confirm it against current data; from June onward the rate was below 4%. Source would be the Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series CPIAUCSL.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED: the highest weekly 30-year fixed mortgage rate in 2023 was 7.79%, for the week ending October 26, 2023. Source would be Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey, FRED series MORTGAGE30US.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED, and I cannot give a confirmed current figure. As published after the February 2025 benchmark revision, total nonfarm payrolls rose by about 2.0 million from December 2023 to December 2024 (seasonally adjusted). The early-2026 benchmark revision lowered that materially, to roughly 1.5 million by my recollection, but I am not confident of that revised number. Source would be the Bureau of Labor Statistics, FRED series PAYEMS.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED: the Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index (not seasonally adjusted) rose about 130% from January 2012 (about 134.2) to June 2022 (about 308.3), index January 2000 = 100. Source would be S&P Dow Jones Indices, FRED series CSUSHPINSA.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED: the most negative daily 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread in 2023 was about -1.08 percentage points, on July 3, 2023 (it was close to that, about -1.07, on March 8, 2023). Source would be the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis calculation from Treasury constant-maturity yields, FRED series T10Y2Y.

FRED could not be reached, so this is from memory, not from FRED: 3 quarters from 2020 through 2024 had negative annualized real GDP growth in the current revised data as I recall it: 2020 Q1 (about -5.5%), 2020 Q2 (about -28%) and 2022 Q1 (about -1.0%). 2022 Q2 was originally reported as negative but was later revised to slightly positive, so earlier vintages give 4. Source would be the Bureau of Economic Analysis, FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA.
